title: The one C keyword that makes a local variable remember
description:
A local variable in C resets every single time its function is called. Mark it `static` and it keeps its value between calls instead — persistence without turning it into a global that any function can touch. Here's a call counter that remembers how many times it ran, straight from Level 1 of the C Mastery Path.

Source lesson:
- https://sigilipelli.github.io/c-mastery-path/level-1/04-functions/

#Shorts

beats.narration: A local variable in C forgets everything the moment its function returns. Call the function again, and it starts back at zero. But add one keyword, and it remembers.
Here's a call counter. The variable calls is marked static, so it's initialized just once. After that it holds onto its value between calls instead of resetting every time.
Call it three times in a row and the count climbs. One, two, three. Same variable, still alive between calls.

display.output:
Called 1 time(s)
Called 2 time(s)
Called 3 time(s)

beats.narration: That's the trick. Unlike a global, a static local is still only visible inside its own function. You get persistence without exposing it to the rest of the file.
